description_full: TD SYNNEX Corporation operates as a distributor and solutions aggregator for the information technology ecosystem in the United States, Europe, and internationally. It offers personal computing devices and peripherals, mobile phones and accessories, printers, and supplies; and data center technologies, such as hybrid cloud, security, storage, networking, servers, software, converged and hyper-converged infrastructure, and hyperscale infrastructure. The company also provides design, integration, test and other production value-added solutions, thermal testing, power-draw efficiency testing, burn-in, quality, and logistics support; logistics and field services; depot repair and customer management services; and cloud services public cloud solutions in productivity and collaboration, infrastructure as a service, platform as a service, software as a service, security, mobility, AI, and other hybrid solutions. In addition, it offers online services; net terms, third party leasing, and floor plan financing and letters-of-credit backed financing and arrangements, as well as lease products to reseller customers and their end-users and provides device-as-a-service to end-users; and direct mail, external media advertising, reseller product training, targeted telemarketing campaigns, national and regional trade shows, trade groups, database analysis, print on demand services, and web-based marketing. It serves resellers, corporate and government resellers, system integrators, direct marketers, retailers, and managed service providers. The company has strategic alliance with EigenQ, Inc. to help public-sector, defense, critical infrastructure and enterprise customers assess and prepare AMD EPYC processor-based server environments for the post-quantum security transition. The company was formerly known as SYNNEX Corporation and changed its name to TD SYNNEX Corporation in September 2021. TD SYNNEX Corporation was founded in 1980 and is headquartered in Fremont, California.

financial_summary: TD SYNNEX Corporation is a large-cap technology business with a $17.3B market cap on $62.5B of annual revenue.
The top line has compounded at +0% over the past three years and +17% annually across the full decade, which puts it in mature, slow-growth territory.

Returns on capital run at 7% against a 10% cost of capital, which means the business is destroying value with every dollar it reinvests, and 7% gross margins are typical of commodity economics where competitors can replicate the product cheaply.

The business throws off $1.4B in free cash flow — roughly 2 cents on every revenue dollar, which is the owner-earnings figure that actually belongs to shareholders, and cash conversion sits at 1.85× so those profits are backed by real cash.
On the balance sheet, leverage is comfortably conservative at 1.2× net debt/EBITDA, and interest coverage runs at 4.0×.

Shareholder yield of 4.3% reflects a genuine commitment to returning capital rather than empire-building, and insiders hold 5.0% of the shares, and profit capture is only 0.1× the fair share, suggesting no structural edge inside its industry.
